title: sources and auth_methods answer the same question in every issued token
description:
hire-grpc/src/service.rs passes the identical expression vec![claim.source().to_owned()] for BOTH HireClaims fields, so in every token hired issues, 'sources' and 'auth_methods' are single-element and identical to each other.

They are supposed to answer different questions. SPEC-HIRE.md:356-366 prints them differing: sources ["tailscale", "piv-smartcard"] is WHERE the identity came from; auth_methods ["tailscale_oidc", "fido2_up"] is HOW the user authenticated. A consumer reading auth_methods to decide whether a hardware authenticator was involved currently reads an attestor name instead.

So the spec documents a token hired cannot issue. This is a behavioural gap, not a typing one: Claim carries a single source() and no separate auth-method list, so closing it needs a richer Claim, which is why it was left out of the .51 refactor -- that pass preserved the behaviour byte for byte.

Related: the transposition hazard named in the HireClaims::new doc comment is unobservable at the current call site precisely because both arguments are the same expression. It becomes real as soon as the two lists diverge.

Found while fixing persona-5s4b.51.
acceptance_criteria: Claim carries auth methods separately from source; the two arrays can differ; a multi-source identity emits more than one entry.
